label: Piano 3w, the GS variation tone, read out of a module's own recordings
audition_title: libsonare Piano 3w vs the module's own recordings
_notes: The GS variation Piano 3w sits at program 2, Bank Select MSB 8; `gm_fallback_map.cpp` voices it apart from its capital and this is the reference that patch is fitted against. The grid sits on the source's own lattice - it holds one recording every three semitones from 24 to 96 and nothing between - at six-semitone steps. The span is the capital capture's compass rounded onto that lattice, so the variation and the tone it is a copy of are read over the same register.
_velocities: One, and 100 is a label rather than a measurement: the font records no velocity and the importer refuses a grid asking for more than one layer. `vel_range` and the dynamics it feeds are excused in `dimensions_na` for that reason.
_dry: Nothing played this, so nothing was switched off. What the file holds is the module's own PCM with no effect in front of it, which is what `source_class: module` asks for.
_stimulus: The gate is the recording itself. Every cell of this grid runs 2.60 to 5.09 s and nothing pads one, so 2600 ms is the longest window all 9 of them hold.
_realtime: Read rather than played: `import_sf2.py` extracts the recorded frames, so there is no host to settle and no lead-in to strip. `preroll_ms` is 0 because a recording begins at its own first frame.
_timbres: One. The source holds exactly one recording per note of this tone, so there is no second of it to disagree with and this capture cannot move the voice past `voiced` however complete its coverage.
_dimensions: Coverage is read against `toneclass.canonical_dimensions`, which for program 2 is 13 dimensions. The four below are what this source cannot carry, each argued from what the font sets rather than from its being a font.

dimensions_na.vel_range: the font declares no velocity layers at all - `velRange` is set on none of its zones, so it holds one recording per note at a velocity it does not state. A grid asking for more than one would write that recording into every row of the axis a dynamics fit reads
dimensions_na.stereo: the recordings are mono (`sampleType` 1) and the font sets no `pan`, so the image is absent by construction rather than by voicing
dimensions_na.register: the font sets no `initialAttenuation` anywhere, so the level relation between one note and the next is not in it. Over this grid the peaks span 3.7 dB, which is the headroom each recording was normalised into rather than the instrument's fall across its compass
dimensions_na.damper: a recording ends where it was cut and carries no note-off, so there is no key lift for a release to be read from

_rig: Unclassified and terminal, which is not the same as unanswered. An electric grand is a strung piano heard through its own pickups, so it is a family that carries an amplifier and the question has to be put; what is missing here is any way to put it. Neither route reaches this source. There is no A/B, because the module has no amplifier stage to switch off - the tone is a recording of whatever chain sampled it, fixed, and nothing downstream of that is a control. The sibling-shape test does not apply either: it turns a dark spectrum into evidence by finding siblings that share the shape, which is an argument only where the siblings came through ONE chain in one session, and this source's tones were each sampled separately. A `none` here would be a claim nothing measured, which is why the acoustic instruments of this source carry one and this tone does not - for a grand or a marimba there is no amplifier for the answer to be about.
_room: The module is recorded with reverb, chorus, delay and the insertion effect all off, and `import_sf2.py --report` plus its own dryness check measure the imported corpus rather than taking this declaration's word for it.
_identity: Which file and which of its presets answered this timbre lives in the untracked sibling `electric_grand_wide.local.json`. Everything here is the method; scoring, fitting and diagnosing read `reference/electric_grand_wide.json`.
